stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Of the more than 5,000 exoplanets confirmed so far, most circle their stars in less than a year. The skew says more about method than about nature: the transit technique finds a planet by the faint dip in starlight it causes when crossing its star, and short orbits repeat those dips often enough for quick confirmation. That makes the planet designated KX-118 b a prized outlier. ______ telescopes monitoring its star continuously for eight years recorded it crossing just once.
explanation: The sentence before the blank says KX-118 b is an outlier, meaning it is not one of the many short-orbit planets that the transit method finds easily. The sentence after gives the proof. If the planet crossed its star only once in eight years of continuous watching, its orbit must be far longer than a year. That is exactly what makes it an outlier. Sentence two confirms and sharpens the claim in sentence one, so you need a word that reinforces: 'Indeed.'

A.why: You reacted to a surface contrast. 'Prized' sounds like good news and 'just once' sounds like a disappointment, so 'Nevertheless' felt right. But the single crossing is the reason the planet counts as an outlier, not something that happens in spite of it. The passage says short orbits produce frequent dips, so a planet that dips only once fits the outlier label exactly. Nothing is being contradicted.

C.why: You correctly saw that the two sentences point the same way, then picked the wrong kind of agreement. 'Moreover' adds a separate, new point, as if the single crossing were a second, independent fact about the planet. In fact, the single crossing is the evidence for the outlier claim. It backs up the claim already made, and that calls for 'Indeed', not a word that adds a new item.

D.why: 'Similarly' needs a second case that is like the first. Both sentences are about the same planet, KX-118 b, and no parallel planet or situation appears. Two sentences that agree are not automatically 'similar' in the sense this word requires.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Hydrologists credit floodplain wetlands with two distinct services to the rivers beside them. When a river overtops its banks, a wetland's spongy soils and dense vegetation absorb much of the overflow, lowering the flood crest that reaches towns downstream. ______ long after the water has receded, plants and microbes in those soils go on stripping nitrogen from what remains, so the water eventually seeping back into the channel is cleaner than the water that arrived.
explanation: The first sentence says wetlands perform two services. The second sentence describes the first one, which is reducing floods. The sentence after the blank describes a different service of the same kind, which is cleaning the water. It is the second item of the pair, separate from the first and parallel to it. A new item that points the same direction needs an addition word: 'In addition.'

A.why: You saw the umbrella phrase 'two distinct services' and expected one member of it to follow as a sample. But the first member was already given in the sentence before the blank. The blank opens the second member, which follows a sibling, not the umbrella sentence. 'For instance' would treat nitrogen removal as an illustration of flood control, and it is not.

B.why: You read a contrast in timing: during the flood versus 'long after the water has receded.' A change of time is not disagreement. Both sentences describe benefits a wetland gives a river, and the second does not undercut or limit the first. If you test it with 'and also', the two sentences read naturally, so this is addition, not contrast.

D.why: You correctly saw that the sentences agree but chose the reinforcing word instead of the adding one. 'Indeed' would require the next sentence to confirm or intensify the flood-control claim. Removing nitrogen says nothing about lowering flood crests. It is a separate service, which the passage says is 'distinct', so it has to be added, not used to strengthen the first point.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Dietitians often describe eggs in terms of a single nutrient: protein. Yet the yolk alone carries two compounds that protein counts overlook. It is one of the richest common sources of choline, which the body uses to build cell membranes. ______ it supplies lutein, a pigment that collects in the retina and helps filter harmful blue light.
explanation: The phrase "two compounds" names a category. The sentence before the blank gives the first compound (choline), and the sentence after gives the second (lutein). The second sentence adds a parallel item to the first and agrees with it, so you need an addition word. "In addition" is the one that does that.

A.why: You spotted the umbrella noun "two compounds" and expected the next sentence to give an example. But the blank doesn't follow the umbrella sentence. It follows the choline sentence, and lutein isn't an example of choline. It's the second member of the pair, set beside the first.

C.why: The "Yet" earlier in the passage put you in a contrasting frame of mind, and lutein is a different nutrient from choline. Being different isn't the same as disagreeing, though. Try putting "and also" between the sentences: it works, so the relationship is addition.

D.why: Lutein being in the yolk isn't a consequence of choline being in the yolk. The two facts sit side by side, and neither causes the other.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most of the 212 burials at the Bronze Age cemetery of Tell Varos hold only a clay pot or two, a pattern that suggests a community with little difference in wealth. Grave 41 is the conspicuous exception: it contains bronze daggers, strings of amber beads, and a gold diadem. ______ not one of the other 211 graves holds even a single object of gold.
explanation: The sentence before the blank claims that Grave 41 is an exception. Pointing out that no other grave has any gold at all shows how much of an exception it is. The sentence after the blank backs up the claim before it, so "Indeed" is the word you need.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. The sentence after the blank switches from Grave 41 back to the plain graves, so it seems to push against the words just before it. What it actually does is confirm the larger point that Grave 41 is an outlier, so nothing is being reversed.

B.why: What Grave 41 contains can't explain why the other graves have no gold. One fact doesn't cause the other.

C.why: The empty graves aren't an instance of Grave 41's riches. The sentence makes the exception stand out more. It doesn't give a sample of it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Contour lines on a topographic map do two jobs at once. Each line joins points of equal elevation, so a hiker can read the height of any spot that falls on it. ______ the spacing between lines shows steepness: lines crowded together mark a cliff, while widely spaced lines mark gentle ground.
explanation: The text says contour lines do "two jobs." The sentence before the blank describes the first job (showing elevation), and the sentence after describes the second (showing steepness). Two separate items that point the same way call for an addition word, which here is "In addition."

A.why: "Specifically" would mean the sentence after the blank restates the elevation job more precisely. Steepness is a different job, and the passage tells you there are two.

B.why: This is the subtype's trap. The sentence after the blank contains its own contrast (crowded lines versus widely spaced ones), and that inside contrast pulls you toward a contrast word. The relationship between the two sentences is still addition.

D.why: "Instead" would mean the second job replaces the first. The passage says the lines do both jobs "at once."

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Woodcut is often dismissed as the crudest of the printmaking methods, since lines gouged with a knife supposedly cannot match the fineness of engraving. The printmakers of Edo-period Japan are the great counterexample. ______ carvers in Edo cut lines in cherry wood fine enough to render single strands of hair, a precision that European printers of the time reached only with engraved copper.
explanation: The sentence before the blank makes a claim: Edo printmakers are a counterexample to the idea that woodcut is crude. The sentence after gives vivid evidence for that same claim. When the second sentence strengthens the first, the word you want is "Indeed."

B.why: This is the subtype's trap. You read the hair-fine lines against "dismissed as the crudest" and saw a reversal. That reversal had already happened in the counterexample sentence. The sentence after the blank agrees with the sentence right before it.

C.why: This gets the order backward. The Edo printmakers count as a counterexample because their carvers worked so finely, not the other way around.

D.why: The mention of Europe made you think the passage was cutting to something happening at the same time somewhere else. But the sentence after the blank is still about Edo, and it's still proving the same point.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Spider silk is often called stronger than steel, and by weight it is: a strand can bear several times the load of a steel wire of equal mass. That comparison, however, actually undersells the material. ______ dragline silk can stretch to roughly a third beyond its resting length before it breaks, absorbing energy that would snap a steel wire stretched by only a few percent.
explanation: The sentence before the blank says that the strength comparison undersells silk. The sentence after shows how: silk also stretches far more than steel before it breaks. The second sentence backs up the claim directly before it, so "Indeed" fits.

A.why: The words "undersells" and "however" made you think the steel comparison was being thrown out and replaced. It isn't. The comparison is incomplete, not wrong, and the next sentence adds to it.

B.why: This is the subtype's trap. The "however" earlier turns away from the strength claim. Once you've noticed that turn, the sentence after the blank keeps going in the new direction and doesn't reverse it a second time.

D.why: Silk's stretch isn't caused by the comparison underselling it. The stretch is the evidence that the comparison undersells silk.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Narrowing a street seems certain to slow traffic, and on Hornby Avenue it did: after two car lanes became protected bike paths, average driving speeds dropped by 8 percent. Yet travel times along the avenue barely changed, since fewer drivers now raced ahead only to idle at the next red light. ______ the number of cyclists using the avenue tripled within a year of the change.
explanation: The sentence before the blank gives one good result of the redesign: travel times held steady. The sentence after gives a separate good result: cycling tripled. A second, parallel point that supports the same case calls for "Moreover."

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. The "Yet" and the falling numbers right before the blank put you in a contrasting mood. Rising cycling doesn't push against steady travel times, though. Both count in favor of the redesign.

C.why: "In other words" would mean the cycling figure restates the travel-time finding. It's a different result about different people.

D.why: "Instead" would mean more cycling happened in place of steady travel times. The passage reports both.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Over a nine-year trial on a Nebraska research farm, adding winter wheat to the usual corn-soybean rotation reduced nitrogen fertilizer use by about 40 percent. Skeptics had expected the savings to come at the expense of the harvest, but yields did not suffer. ______ corn grown in the three-crop plots outyielded corn in the two-crop plots in seven of the nine seasons.
explanation: The sentence before the blank claims that yields didn't suffer. The sentence after goes further in the same direction: yields actually improved. When the second sentence strengthens the first, "In fact" is the word you want.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. "Did not suffer" sounds negative, and "outyielded" sounds like a turn away from it. Both sentences make the same point, and the second just makes it more strongly.

B.why: You noticed that both sentences point the same way, but you took the wrong member of the family. "Similarly" lines up two parallel cases. Here the second sentence strengthens the first claim and doesn't describe a separate case like it.

C.why: The higher corn yields aren't caused by yields not suffering. The second sentence is the strongest evidence for the first, not a result of it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Pirahã, a language spoken along the Maici River in Brazil, has drawn linguists' attention chiefly for what it reportedly lacks. Researchers have described it as having no words for exact quantities, not even one for "one." ______ it is said to have no basic color terms, so speakers describe a hue by comparison instead, calling something "like blood" rather than red.
explanation: The passage frames Pirahã by "what it reportedly lacks." The sentence before the blank gives one gap (number words), and the sentence after gives another (color terms). A second, parallel gap that points the same way calls for "Moreover."

B.why: This is the subtype's trap. The "instead" and "rather than" inside the color sentence make it sound contrastive. But having no color terms agrees with having no number terms: both are things the language lacks.

C.why: Having no number words doesn't cause a language to have no color words. The passage presents the two gaps as separate facts.

D.why: You saw the umbrella phrase "what it reportedly lacks" and reached for a word that names a specific case. "Namely" would make the color sentence a restatement of the number sentence. It's a separate item, not the same one said more precisely.
